text:
The clearest anomaly is M5, the tail device. Its drain sits at about 0.225 V, below its 0.546 V Vdsat, so it is in triode. The diff-pair common-mode level (Vcm = 0.9 V minus Vgs ≈ 0.675 V) forces that low tail voltage, so M5 cannot stay in saturation with its current size. This collapses the DC gain (20.7 dB) and distorts the integrator's loop response, which fits the -14.8 dB/dec slope and the f_unity miss. M5's current also sits well below its saturated value for its W/L ratio, which points to a wrong width. M8 is second: its current tracks the M6 reference, so the mirror ratio is intact, but it dominates the f_unity sensitivity. R1 is third: it has the largest sensitivity, but its value is not obviously inconsistent with the design.
